([[Summerlin, Nevada]]) | college = [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] (2016–2017) | draft_year = 2017 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 10 | draft_team = [[Sacramento Kings]] | career_start = 2017 | years1 = {{nbay|2017|start}}–{{nbay|2020|end}} | team1 = [[Portland Trail Blazers]] | years2 = {{nbay|2021|start}}–{{nbay|2024|end}} | team2 = [[San Antonio Spurs]] | years3 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2022]] | team3 = →[[Austin Spurs]] | years4 = {{nbay|2024|end}}–present | team4 = [[Chicago Bulls]] | highlights = * Second-team All-[[West Coast Conference|WCC]] (2017) * WCC All-Freshman Team (2017) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2016 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2016]]) }} '''Zach Collins''' (born November 19, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Chicago Bulls]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]]. He was drafted by the [[Sacramento Kings]] with the 10th overall pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]] and was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] on draft night. During his earlier career with the team he battled many injuries causing him to only play in 154 games in his first four seasons. He joined the [[San Antonio Spurs]] as a free agent in August 2021, where he played for four seasons before being traded to the Bulls in 2025. ==High school career== Collins played high school basketball at [[Bishop Gorman High School]] in [[Summerlin, Nevada]], where he helped to lead his school to four consecutive state championships.{{Cite web |title=With latest state title, Bishop Gorman sets new Nevada mark for championships |url=http://lasvegassun.com/news/2016/feb/26/with-latest-state-title-bishop-gorman-sets-new-nev/ |date=February 26, 2016 |work=[[Las Vegas Sun]] |access-date=May 19, 2019 |first1=Ray |last1=Brewer}} For his first three seasons at Bishop Gorman, Collins came off the bench and played alongside fellow seven-footers and McDonald's All-Americans [[Stephen Zimmerman]] and [[Chase Jeter]].{{cite web|title=RECRUITING: Bishop Gorman's Collins commits to Gonzaga|url=http://nevadapreps.com/boys-basketball/recruiting-bishop-gorman-s-collins-commits-gonzaga|date=March 16, 2015}}{{cite web|title=Zach Collins Is Serious About 3x3|url=http://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2015/06/zach-collins-is-serious-about-3x3.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905211851/http://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2015/06/zach-collins-is-serious-about-3x3.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 5, 2015|date=June 5, 2015}} Collins had a productive senior year, averaging 17.3 points, 14 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 6.4 blocked shots on his way to the most valuable player of Nevada's Southwest League{{cite web|title=Nevada Boys Basketball POY: Zach Collins|url=http://nevadapreps.com/boys-basketball/2016-all-state-boys-basketball-teams|date=March 17, 2016}} and the Nevada Gatorade Player of the Year award.{{cite web|title=Nevada Boys Basketball POY: Zach Collins|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2016/gatorade-nevada-boys-basketball-poy-zach-collins|date=March 17, 2016}} Collins also broke Nevada's single-season record for most rebounds and blocked shots during his senior season.{{cite web|title=2016 7'0 C Zach Collins; Bishop Gorman (NV) Breaks single season record in rebounds and blocks for the state of Nevada. Collins is a PRO|url=https://twitter.com/PremierBall/status/703472074954661888|date=February 26, 2016}} In the summer of 2015, Collins competed in the [[FIBA 3x3 Under-18 World Championships]], where he teamed up with [[Jalek Felton]], [[Payton Pritchard]] and [[P. J. Washington]] and won the USA tournament. His team moved on to represent the US at the 2015 World Championship in Debrecen, Hungary, where they finished in eighth place.{{cite web|title=USA Basketball Profile: Zach Collins|url=http://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/c/collins-zach.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150702121110/http://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/c/collins-zach.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 2, 2015|access-date=April 4, 2016}} His team advanced to the final 16 where they defeated Poland, but then lost a close game to France, featuring fellow Gonzaga commit [[Killian Tillie]], in the quarterfinals.{{cite web|title=FIBA 3x3 Profile: Zach Collins|url=http://www.3x3planet.com/en/PlayerProfile?playerFibaId=PLW15EQGEOKWIUSA|access-date=April 4, 2016}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 3, 2015|access-date=April 4, 2016}} Despite being rated as a four-star prospect, Collins was named to the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2016 McDonald's All-American Game]].{{cite web|title=McDonald's All American Zach Collins is big man with will to move the ball|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2016/hometown-heroes-mcdonalds-all-american-zach-collins-is-big-man-with-will-to-move-the-ball|date=January 21, 2016}} Collins was the first McDonald's All-American to commit to Gonzaga out of high school, but three other McDonald's All-American transferred to Gonzaga after attending other colleges: [[Micah Downs]], [[Kyle Wiltjer]] and [[Nigel Williams-Goss]].{{cite web|title=McDonald's notes: Las Vegas 7-footer Zach Collins is first Gonzaga commit in All-American game|website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/highschool/ct-spt-0329-prep-bbk-mcdonalds-bits-20160328-story.html|date=March 28, 2016}} Collins helped to lead the West squad to a 114–107 win in the while scoring nine points, along with six rebounds, three assists and two steals on 3-for-5 field goals and 1-for-2 three-pointers in 12 minutes of play.{{cite web|title=Gorman's Collins fuels victory in All American game|url=http://nevadapreps.com/boys-basketball/gorman-s-collins-fuels-victory-all-american-game|date=March 30, 2016}} ===Recruiting=== In the winter of 2015, during Collins' junior year in high school, he took official visits to California, San Diego State, Utah, New Mexico and Gonzaga, as well as unofficial visits to UNLV.{{cite web|title=Collins to get spotlight on him|url=https://basketballrecruiting.n.rivals.com/news/collins-to-get-spotlight-on-him|date=March 6, 2015|access-date=April 4, 2016|archive-date=April 13, Collins committed to Gonzaga.{{cite web|title=Zach Collins commits to Zags|url=http://www.spokesman.com/blogs/sportslink/2015/mar/16/colllins-commits-zags/|date=March 16, 2015}} He signed with the occasionally in tandem—with fifth-year senior center [[Przemek Karnowski]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2017/04/01/gonzaga-south-carolina-zach-collins-final-four|title=The one national semifinal game of the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]], Collins registered 14 points, 13 rebounds and six blocks, as the Bulldogs defeated [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]], 77–73, sending them to their first national championship game.{{Cite by freshman Zach Collins at Final Four|work=USA TODAY|access-date=April 3, 2017|language=en}} ==Professional career== ===Portland Trail Blazers (2017–2021)=== At the conclusion of his freshman season, Collins announced his intention to forgo his final three years of college eligibility and enter the [[2017 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=http://www.spokesman.com/stories/2017/apr/11/gonzagas-zach-collins-declares-for-nba-draft-inten/|title=Gonzaga's Zach Collins declares for NBA Draft, intends to hire agent |website=Spokesman.com|author=Jim Meehan|date=April 11, 2017|access-date=April 11, 2017}} He was drafted 10th overall by the [[Sacramento Kings]] and subsequently traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{Cite news |last=Conway |first=Tyler |date=June 23, 2017 |title=Zach Collins Picked No. 10 in NBA Draft, Kings Trade Him to Blazers |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2704075-kings-pick-zach-collins-no-10-in-nba-draft-expected-to-be-traded-to-blazers |access-date=January 5, 2025 |work=Bleacher Report |language=en-US}}{{cite web |date=June 22, 2017 |title=Trail Blazers Acquire Draft Rights to Zach Collins |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-acquire-draft-rights-zach-collins |access-date=January 5, 2025 |work=NBA.com}} On July 3, 2017, Collins signed with the Trail Blazers.{{cite web |date=July 3, 2017 |title=TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN ZACH COLLINS |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-zach-collins |access-date=January 5, 2025 |work=NBA.com}} On November 5, 2019, the Trail Blazers announced that Collins had undergone successful surgery in repairing his left labrum and was expected to be sidelined for about four months.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2019/11/5/zach-collins-undergoes-successful-shoulder-surgery|title=ZACH COLLINS UNDERGOES SUCCESSFUL SHOULDER SURGERY|date=November 5, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 5, 2019}} On December 30, 2020, the Trail Blazers announced that Collins had undergone successful surgery in repairing his left medial [[malleolus]] [[stress fracture]],{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/zach-collins-undergoes-ankle-surgery|title=ZACH COLLINS UNDERGOES ANKLE SURGERY|date=December 30, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 30, 2020}} and as result he missed the entire season.{{Cite web|last=Hostetler|first=L.|date=2021-06-29|title=Zach Collins Fractures Foot Again|url=https://www.blazersedge.com/2021/6/29/22556076/portland-trail-blazers-zach-collins-fractures-foot-again|access-date=2021-07-25|website=Blazer's Edge}}{{Cite web|title=Trail Blazers' Zach Collins: Re-fractures foot|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/trail-blazers-zach-collins-re-fractures-foot/|access-date=2021-07-25|website=CBSSports.com|date=June 29, 2021 }} As he was recovering from his previous injury, Collins refractured his foot, and on June 29, 2021, the Trail Blazers announced that he underwent a second revision surgery to repair his left medial malleolus stress fracture.{{Cite web|title=Blazers' Zach Collins (ankle) undergoes surgery|url=https://www.nba.com/news/report-blazers-zach-collins-re-injures-foot|access-date=2021-07-25|website=NBA.com}} He did not appear in the playoffs as a result of the injury. ===San Antonio / Austin Spurs (2021–2025)=== On August 11, 2021, Collins signed a three-year, $22 million contract with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|title=Spurs sign Zach Collins|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-zach-collins|date=August 11, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 11, 2021}} On January 16, 2022, he was assigned to the [[Austin Spurs]] of the [[NBA G League]], while recovering from his ankle injury.{{Cite web|title=SAN ANTONIO ASSIGNS ZACH COLLINS TO AUSTIN SPURS|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/san-antonio-assigns-zach-collins-austin-spurs|access-date=January 17, 2022|website=NBA G League}} On January 31, he was recalled.{{Cite web|title=Zach Collins recalled to Spurs Monday|url=https://www.fantasypros.com/nba/news/340216/zach-collins-recalled-to-spurs-monday.php|access-date=February 4, 2022|website=FantasyPros|date=January 31, 2022 }} He made his Spurs debut February 4 against the Houston Rockets, scoring 10 points and grabbing seven rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.thescore.com/nba/news/2292092|title=Spurs' Collins makes immediate impact in 1st game since NBA bubble|last=Winick|first=Matthew|date=February 4, 2022|work=The Score|access-date=February 6, 2022}} On February 10, 2023, Collins scored 29 points and grabbed 11 rebounds during a 138–131 double-overtime loss against the [[Detroit Pistons]].[https://www.fantasypros.com/nba/news/391926/zach-collins-takes-advantage-playing-time-with-monster-game-friday Zach Collins takes advantage of playing time with monster game Friday]{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} During the 2022–23 season, Collins improved his statistical averages, in total averaging nearly 12 points per game, three assists per game and shooting 52% from the field and 37% from three.{{citation needed|date=June 2023}} On October 22, 2023, Collins signed a two-year $35 million contract extension with the Spurs.{{Cite web |date=2023-10-22 |title=Report: Zach Collins, Spurs finalizing 2-year, $35 million contract extension |url=https://www.nba.com/news/spurs-zach-collins-contract-extension-2023 |access-date=2023-10-22 |website=NBA.com}} He played in 69 games (starting 29) during the [[2023–24 NBA season|2023–24 season]] for the Spurs, averaging 11.2 points, 5.4 rebounds and 2.8 assists. In the team's season finale on April 14, 2024, against the [[Detroit Pistons]], Collins suffered a dislocated right shoulder. After an [[magnetic resonance imaging|MRI]] revealed a torn labrum, he underwent surgery to repair to injury.{{Cite web|title=Spurs' Zach Collins to undergo surgery on torn right labrum|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39970206/spurs-zach-collins-undergo-surgery-torn-right-labrum|access-date=April 22, 2024|website=espn.com}} ===Chicago Bulls (2025–present)=== On February 3, 2025, Collins, alongside [[Tre Jones]] and a 2025 first-round pick, was traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in a three team deal, in which they sent [[Sidy Cissoko]], three first-round picks and two second-round picks to the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|title=Bulls acquire Kevin Huerter, Zach Collins and Tre Jones in three-team deal|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-acquire-kevin-huerter-zach-collins-and-tre-jones-in-three-team-deal|website=NBA.com|date=February 3, 2025|access-date=February 3, 2025}} In 28 appearances (eight starts) for Chicago, he averaged 8.6 points, 6.7 rebounds, and 2.1 assists. On October 18, 2025, it was announced that Collins would miss at least one month after suffering a non-displaced fracture in his left wrist.{{cite web | last=Haslett | first=Jack | title=Chicago Bulls Center Zach Collins Receives Unfortunate Injury News | website=Chicago Bulls On SI | date=2025-10-18 | url=https://www.si.com/nba/bulls/onsi/news/chicago-bulls-center-zach-collins-receives-unfortunate-injury-news | access-date=2025-12-09}} In 10 appearances prior to the injury, he averaged 9.7 points, 5.6 rebounds, and 1.5 assists. On February 21, 2026, the Bulls announced that Collins would require season-ending right toe surgery.{{Cite web|title=Bulls' Zach Collins to undergo season-ending toe surgery; Jaden Ivey out 2 weeks|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7062343/2026/02/21/bulls-zach-collins-toe-surgery-nba/|access-date=February 23, 2026|website=nytimes.com|language=en}} On June 30, 2026, Collins signed a
